title: The importance of leadership in change

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the importance of leadership in change: the leadership style point covers decision-making styles, and the managing change point covers the broader steps of managing change, including goals and training, rather than why leaders matter to it.

draft.title: The importance of leadership in change
card: Leadership is guiding and influencing people towards a goal. In change, leaders set the direction: they decide what the business is moving towards.
Leaders explain why the change is needed. When staff understand the reason, such as falling sales or a new competitor, they are more likely to accept it.
Leaders keep staff on board through the change. They listen to concerns, give support and keep talking with staff until the change is settled.
Without this leadership, staff may feel unsure or left out. They may then resist the change, which can slow it down or cause it to fail.
draft.remember: Good leaders point the way, give the reason and bring staff along.

a.q: A manager tells staff that a new ordering system is coming because the old one keeps losing orders. Which leadership role is this?
opts: Explaining why the change is needed
Setting the direction of the change
Keeping staff on board by giving support
Reducing the costs of the change
a.why: The manager gives the reason for the change, which is the faulty system. This is different from setting the direction, which would be deciding where the business is heading. It is also not support, because no help or listening is described.
a.clue: The manager is giving a reason.

b.q: Tariq owns a bakery in Geelong and is moving it to online orders only. He announces the date and says nothing more. Staff become anxious and some start to resist. Which leadership step was missing?
opts: Explaining why and listening to staff concerns
Choosing a clear direction for the business
Setting a date for when the change begins
Making sure the change is a popular one
b.why: Tariq set a direction and a date, but did not give the reason or hear staff concerns. This left staff unsure, so they resisted. Direction was not missing, because online orders only is a clear aim.
b.clue: Tariq already chose where the business is heading.

a.best: Explaining why the change is needed

b.best: Explaining why and listening to staff concerns

problems.detail: The clue 'The manager is giving a reason' maps almost word for word onto the option 'Explaining why the change is needed', so it gives the answer away rather than prompting thought.
